newsitem.title: USA: International Nursing unit options returned.
newsitem.headline: International Nursing unit options returned.

text.p: International Nursing Services Inc said on Tuesday it had reached an agreement with private shareholders to return unit options that were granted to the shareholders last year so as to reduce the number of the company's fully diluted common shares.
A total of 244 unit options were issued in 1996 and 204 unit options will be returned to the company, International Nursing said in a statement.
The unit options returned will be canceled by the company, it added, reducing its fully diluted common shares by more than 6,000,000 shares.
As a part of the return of the unit options the company agreed to reduce the exercise price of the warrants issued pursuant to the 1996 subscription agreements from $2.50 to $0.625.
"We have been working at reducing the number of fully-diluted shares available in the marketplace. This agreement is a positive step in that direction," said company chief executive, John Yeros.
The options were granted to shareholders after a subscription agreement dated July 18, September 13 and September 18 of 1996.
International Nursing provides nursing, rehabilitation and other medical personnel for flexible staffing in home care and other health care facilities.
